summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT), NY with embedded systems and firmware experience on STM32 Cortex-M4 microcontrollers. Built bare-metal C/C++ firmware with direct peripheral programming (GPIO, timers, ADC) and UART/I2C/SPI interfaces, plus real-time control with FreeRTOS and interrupts. Designed PCBs in EAGLE and debugged hardware with oscilloscopes and logic analyzers.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi and HC-05 Bluetooth to translate 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands, with firmware-level sensor handling.
Implemented a custom tap-detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding; resolved sensor jitter through software calibration and resolution tuning.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback.
Led a 25-member robotics team across national competitions, owning PCB fabrication, wiring, and hardware/software integration.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Built a Cortex-M4 temperature monitoring firmware in embedded C with timer-synchronized sensing and real-time display.
Implemented timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture, and a low-level I2C driver.
Programmed peripherals directly in bare-metal C (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1); achieved 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at deterministic 1 Hz update rate; verified in Proteus.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Implemented multi-servo PWM control on STM32 with interrupt-driven UART commands from a Jetson running YOLOv8 object tracking, with user override.
Used FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination; integrated VL53L0X ToF sensing and OLED distance visualization.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Built a voice-controlled robotic pick-and-place system with a Jetson+Arduino controller linked over a WebSocket (TCP/IP) fabric; achieved 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials) at ~11.5s end-to-end latency.
Integrated dual VL53L0X ToF sensors over a TCA9548A I2C mux for contact-aware grasping (gripper close at 25 mm); implemented two-link IK on Arduino in C++ driving five servos.
Resolved 11 integration failures (servo brown-out, false-positive detections) through hardware debugging; deployed the controller bridge as a systemd service with static IP networking.

projects.name: Robocon Competition Robot — Holonomic Drive & Encoder Odometry
bullets: Implemented interrupt-driven quadrature decoding from first principles (4-bit A/B transition state machine) on Arduino Due and drove four motor channels at 15 kHz PWM with 2400 CPR encoder odometry.
